text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-The Social Security Office paid 14,200 people 270 million crowns too much in pensions in 1996. The office says increased pressure and lack of resources have increased mispayments.
-Some 250,000 Norwegians experience violent incidents each year. However, only one in four counties have set up measures to reduce violence or council victims.

-The tourist industry fears that the recent strengthening of the crown will reduce the number of tourists coming to Norway. According to industry analyses, Germans in particular are likely to choose other places for their holidays.
-Despite the authorities' decision not to intervene in the foreign exchange market to dampen appreciation in the crown, the Labour Union has decided to show moderation in this year wage negotiations.
-A Labour Party spokesman suggests 40 billion crowns should be spent on upgrading the railway system over the next ten years. It is time to put more emphasis on maintenance, the spokesman says.
